sources.quote: The Canadian Veterinary Medical Association counts roughly 4,300 accredited veterinary facilities and just over 15,000 actively practising veterinarians nationally
sources.title: Statistics | CVMA
sources.evidence: In 2024 there were 16,317 registered veterinarians, 15,278 actively-practicing veterinarians, and 4,328 accredited facilities across Canada.

sources.quote: The Canadian Animal Health Institute counts roughly 7.2 million dogs and 8.2 million cats, in more than half of Canadian households
sources.title: Canadian Pet Population Survey | Canadian Animal Health Institute (CAHI)
sources.evidence: In 2024, Canada was home to an estimated 7.2 million dogs and 8.2 million cats, making pets an integral part of more than half of Canadian households. The survey is conducted biennially by Kynetec on behalf of CAHI.

sources.quote: the Veterinary Professionals Act, 2024, which received Royal Assent in June 2024 and still awaits proclamation
sources.title: College of Veterinarians of Ontario - Legislation
sources.evidence: The new Veterinary Professionals Act received Royal Assent on June 6, 2024. While the Veterinary Professionals Act is now law, it is not yet in full effect. Implementation will occur in two stages; the College is currently in stage one, the transition stage. The Act limits use of the titles veterinary technician and registered veterinary technician to individuals licensed with the College, and the earliest the new model could be in place is currently estimated to be January 2027.

sources.quote: Google Local Services Ads, the badged pay per lead format, covers only home service categories in Canada
sources.title: Getting started with Local Services Ads - Canada - Local Services Help
sources.evidence: Local Services Ads in Canada are available only for certain service categories, including appliance repair services, carpet cleaning services, cleaning services, electricians, HVAC, junk removal services, lawn care services, locksmiths, movers, pest control services, plumbers, roofers, tree services, and water damage services.

sources.quote: NAPHIA reports insured pets in Canada in the mid hundreds of thousands
sources.publisher: North American Pet Health Insurance Association
sources.title: Total Pets Insured - NAPHIA State of the Industry Report
sources.evidence: Approximately 9% of the 7.03 million insured pets across North America in 2024 are based in Canada, roughly 632,700 insured pets. In Canada, 2024 ended with the penetration rate for dogs at 5.57%, and cats at 1.76%.

sources.quote: to veterinarians certified by a recognized specialty board
sources.title: College of Veterinarians of Ontario - Licensure
sources.evidence: A veterinarian in Ontario cannot use the term specialist unless they are Board-certified in a specialty recognized by the College. To describe oneself as a specialist, when one is not, is considered professional misconduct. Stating one has a specialty in a field is considered to be claiming specialist status.

sources.quote: bans testimonials of support or gratitude and requires advertised fees to be precise and honoured for the stated period
sources.title: M-8, r. 4 - Code de déontologie des médecins vétérinaires
sources.evidence: The veterinarian cannot, in their advertising, use or permit the use of a testimonial of support or recognition. Veterinarians must indicate whether additional services not included in advertised fees could be required, and all fees or prices must remain in effect for a minimum period of 90 days after their last dissemination or publication.

sources.quote: holds registrants responsible for work an agency does for them
sources.publisher: College of Veterinarians of British Columbia
sources.title: Advertising Do's and Dont's – College of Veterinarians of BC
sources.evidence: Registrants are responsible for ensuring that any communication they permit to be published, displayed, distributed, or used relating to their professional or ancillary services adheres to the advertising provisions in the Bylaws (Part 4, Division 4.4). The marketing and advertising for your facility is the responsibility of the designated registrant, unless the owner of the facility has delegated marketing and advertising to another registrant.
